(1) Built pre-fix tree in a detached git worktree at RED commit ec18da8da6 (symlinked packages/main and root node_modules to the shared repo node_modules; tsc emits despite unrelated 'ws' type errors since noEmitOnError is unset), confirmed the emitted dist/core/done-prepare-generated-metadata.js still has the bare execFileSync-no-maxBuffer + catch{return null}, and ran the committed RED test against it: 6 of 8 sections genuinely FAIL, including the 1,400,000-byte commit section reporting the exact misleading reason "verified metadata changed after manifest verification" -- reproducing the incident transcript verbatim. Cleaned up the scratch worktree afterward (git worktree remove). (2) Ran both commands from the brief against the fixed tree: red-b3434-blob-buffer-ceiling.mjs -> PASS (8/8 sections); validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.js -> PASS (7/7 sections). (3) Traced both call sites of isolatedBlobHash/treeBlobHash: both flow only through verifyMetadataBlobDigests -> classifyMetadataBlobDigestComparison, which returns read.kind (absent/unreadable) before ever touching the expected digest -- structurally impossible to report match on a failed read. RED section 6 sweeps expected over 4 values including undefined and gets unreadable/absent every time. (4) Confirmed by grep that the literal string "verified metadata changed after manifest verification" is preserved verbatim for genuine digest mismatches in both the isolated-index and isolated-tree comparison branches (not deleted), while unreadable/absent get their own distinct sentences ("verified metadata could not be read from the..." / "verified metadata is absent from the..."); RED sections 7-8 confirm behaviourally. (5) Independently reproduced the ENOBUFS/empty-truthy-stderr-Buffer claim with two standalone probes outside the test suite: a synthetic oversized child process AND a real "git show" on an oversized blob with a tiny maxBuffer (matching the exact execFileSync call shape used in the module) -- both confirm err.code equals ENOBUFS, err.stderr is an empty but truthy Buffer (length 0), and the naive stderr-or-stdout-or-message idiom renders an empty string. Ran describeChildProcessFailure's logic verbatim against the real error object and confirmed it correctly renders "ENOBUFS: <content>" by filtering empty candidates before selecting. Also independently confirmed via two more real-git probes that the absent-vs-unreadable regex patterns match real git stderr output verbatim, and that a normal nonzero git exit leaves err.code undefined (so it is never misclassified as absent through the nodeLevelFailure gate) while ENOBUFS always sets err.code so it can never be misclassified as absent. (6) Confirmed via the smoke test's own assertions (which I executed, not just read) that a 100-command/12,000-char artifact (measured 1,212,174 bytes) classifies within_budget, bounded=false, output equals JSON.stringify(result) byte-for-byte, and formatValidationEvidenceAdvisory returns null -- today's repository shape is provably a no-op. No fail-open path found anywhere in the diff; no blocking findings.

Confirmed all three of my own findings by execution, not re-reading. F-031: wrote an adversarial probe using the real StoryStore.writeTestEvidence against a scratch dir; reported fileBytes equalled bytes on disk. Pushed harder than the shipped smoke's toJSON-flips-on-call-3 fixture: a toJSON already large on call 1 (converges to a stable admitted record via the reduction loop, bytes on disk still matched); a 3-level nested Proxy with distinct per-level call counters; a value with only Symbol.toPrimitive (confirmed JSON.stringify never invokes it, 0 calls observed, and the returned copy carries no live symbol trap); a top-level getter returning a fresh object on every read (returned record has no accessor descriptor, 200 repeat reads identical). Found no second opinion left in the returned graph in any case. Verified the snapshot lands on all four dispositions via the real store: unmodified, reduced and verdict_only all wrote bytes matching fileBytes; refused correctly never reaches a write (that guard lives in verifier.ts, separately confirmed). F-032: probed all four internal measureWith call sites (the non-object branch and the verdictOnlyRecord fallback, both outside the try; the reduction measure callback and the post-reduction remeasure, both inside it) with throwing builders -- none let an exception escape boundPersistedValidationEvidence; all report record=null, disposition=refused, withinBound=false. Confirmed the three verifier.ts write sites (reusedBound, fallbackBound, persistedBound) each guard on record===null with no cast, and npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/main is clean, so the narrowing is compiler-verified, not just visually plausible. F-030: confirmed an oversized array is refused (not verdict_only), and that null and a small array are unaffected by the added Array.isArray branch. Cost judgement: right and acceptable. Re-ran the real dist smoke (17.9s wall, matching the disclosed 9.9s->18.5s within run-to-run noise) and microbenchmarked boundPersistedValidationEvidence directly outside the smoke harness (~17ms/call for a 100-command shape, ~230ms/call for the 400-command quote-heavy torture fixture) -- same order of magnitude as disclosed, no exaggeration. This path runs exactly once per lattice validate, after the validate commands themselves have already run for seconds to minutes, so tens of ms (realistic shape) to low hundreds of ms (synthetic MB-scale torture fixtures far above realistic evidence size) is negligible. The uniform-everywhere design (vs snapshotting only the returned record, ~7x cheaper) is the right call: this story's whole defect class (F-014, F-027, and now F-031 itself) is exactly a gate that measures one computation and a writer that persists a different one: reintroducing a cheap/authoritative split for intermediate search steps would recreate a smaller instance of that same wedge. Ran and confirmed all five requested commands green: npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/main (clean, 0 errors), red-b3434-blob-buffer-ceiling.mjs (PASS), dist/tasks/validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.js (PASS), test:done-prepare-auto-closeout-smoke (passed), dist/tasks/validation-evidence-reuse-smoke.js (PASS). No blockers. All 32 findings on this story remain resolved.

Converted pass-only finding_add record: measurePersistedEvidenceBytes docstring (validation-executor.ts:650-653, new prose in 036d69edb3) claims: "This duplicates a format owned by core/store.ts, which is outside this storys allowed scope. The coupling is real and is the weak point of this design: if store.ts changes its serialisation, this measurement drifts low and the bound silently loosens. The smoke pins the format so the drift fails a test rather than a phase gate." The final sentence is false as written: no test in the repository exercises core/store.ts serialization at all. validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.ts never imports StoryStore or core/store.js (grep confirms zero references); its two readFileSync calls (lines 532, 671) read handlers/verifier.ts source text only, for unrelated wiring checks. Section 3 (lines 220-227), the only test touching measurePersistedEvidenceBytes format fidelity, computes its own `expected` value via `Buffer.byteLength(`${JSON.stringify(record, null, 2)}\n`, utf8)` -- the SAME literal formula duplicated (not derived from store.ts) inside the test file itself -- then asserts measurePersistedEvidenceBytes(record) equals that independently-derived number. This is a self-consistency check between two hardcoded copies of the same formula (one in core/validation-executor.ts, one in the smoke), not a pin against store.ts. grep for measurePersistedEvidenceBytes, VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_BOUND_BYTES and VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_READ_CEILING_BYTES across packages/main/src and packages/main/tests confirms these symbols are referenced only by validation-executor.ts, verifier.ts and the smoke -- no test anywhere writes a record through the real StoryStore.writeTestEvidence and compares the resulting on-disk byte length to this prediction. If core/store.ts core/store.ts:163 (`JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) + \n`) ever changes its serialisation, both the source formula and the smokes independently-hardcoded expected formula would drift together and stay equal to each other, so every existing assertion would continue to pass while the real file on disk silently diverges from what boundPersistedValidationEvidence counted -- exactly the "measurement drifts low and the bound silently loosens" failure the same docstring names one sentence earlier, with no test catching it. This is not a behavioural defect today (the byte count is currently accurate, verified by running validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.js and red-b3434-blob-buffer-ceiling.mjs, both PASS), and it is candidly disclosed as an accepted out-of-scope coupling elsewhere in the same docstring and in the round-8 commit message ("core/store.ts is out of scope, so the stability comes from the value rather than the writer"). The defect is narrowly the closing sentence overstating what protection exists: it should say the smoke pins this modules OWN duplicated formula for internal self-consistency, and that a drift in store.ts real serialisation is caught by nothing in this repository today (only by a later phase-gate wedge, which is the exact outcome the sentence claims is avoided).
